events.means: A firmware task hung and the watchdog rebooted the ring. Measurements in progress are lost and repeated resets drain the battery. In every sample it came seconds after `hub ful` (hub queue full), at 95% battery.
events.detect: `power on` whose preceding `Reset Status Register` has bit 0x40 set, or `WDT isr save` within the 60 lines before it. Put the WDT task, stack watermark (W) and free heap (H) in properties.

events.means: The ring lost power while the battery was not empty: battery contact, PMIC or board fault. The clock restarts at its default date, so the next hours of data are mis-dated.
events.detect: `power on` with register 0x86 (power-on + brown-out), no `HUB_MSG_POWER_OFF`, `enter shipping mode` or `no_bind off` in the 60 lines before, and the last battery reading (rbc= / val:) above 5%.

events.means: Supply voltage dipped (a motor or radio peak on a weak battery) and reset the MCU without a full power loss.
events.detect: `power on` with brown-out bit 0x04 set and power-on bit 0x02 clear.

events.means: A software reset nobody asked for, typically an assert or fault handler. This is what separates a crash from a planned reboot.
events.detect: `power on` with register 0x08 (software reset) and none of `hub_restart_save`, `fac_reboot_save`, `default_reset_save`, `apprequest_reset`, `ota_ok_save`, `lpm_save`, `sys idle reboot` or `cmd: 24` in the 60 lines before.

events.means: Battery ADC reading was abnormal, so the firmware restarted the system. In the 2025 samples one ring did this 316 times, a reboot loop around 20% battery.
events.detect: `unchg: reinit adc` or `chg: reinit adc`, followed by `hub_restart_save` and a reboot.

events.means: Heap exhausted: the operation is dropped (BLE send, sleep save, GoMore, storage). A precursor to watchdog resets and lost data.
